newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to finalise Sabah power deal on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to finalise Sabah power deal on Wednesday.

text.p: The Malaysian government will finalise the partners of a consortium to take over the privatisation of the Sabah Electricity Board (SEB) on Wednesday, Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Monday.
Moggie was quoted as saying by the national news agency Bernama that the meeting on Wednesday would also finalise the actual level of participation of the consortium members.
He said state power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd would lead the consortium, which would also include the Sabah state government and probably two other entities.
SEB's privatisation could not wait any longer because the power supply situation in Sabah state on Borneo island was quite critical, Moggie said.
"Tenaga Nasional has been chosen to lead the consortium members because we are quite confident that it has the experience and the capacity to do it in the shortest possible time," he told reporters.
"We have already made decision...its a matter of consulting with them formally before we formalise the arrangement."
Moggie did not name the other two partners in the consortium but said that the companies are directly involved in the electricity industry.
The biggest challenge for the consortium was to immediately upgrade power supply in Sabah as there have been many reports of supply disruptions and related problems, he said.
Moggie said SEB's privatisation would also entail complete restructuring of electricity supply management in Sabah.
